summary: Ryuta Kikutani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and others. He served as an assistant at Marburg (~1981–1983) and as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1983; emeritus 1995–2012).
Ryō Nishimura (1972–2016) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1995) and under Fumihiko Sueki (~1995–2004).

Ryōjin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa. He was a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and Otani University, later becoming Otani's president (1961–1967).

Ryōshō Tanaka (1933–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. He served as a professor, dean, and president at Komazawa University, and also held posts at Ryukoku University and the Soto Zen Research Center.
Ryōshū Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama. He held a lecturer post at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Ryōō (1856–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji and Koyasan University.

Ryūjō Yamada (1895–1979) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1925–1943), Tohoku University (~1943–1959), and Musashino Joshi Gakuin/Musashino University.
Ryūzan Nishimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Rüdiger Schmitt is an Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar who studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1958–1965). He held a post at Saarland University from ~1972 to 2004.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History.

S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at SPG College and the University of Madras, served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and held professorships at Presidency College, Chennai, and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri (1859–1906) was an Indologist who studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras (~1878–1881). He served as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1883–1888).

S. N. Balagangadhara is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at National College, Bangalore, and Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch. He served as a director at Ghent University (~1991–2018) and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
S. N. Savadi is an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested in 1953 and 1969).

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri (1893–1942) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942) at the University of Madras.

S. Sankaranarayanan (1926–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He served as Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre until 1999 and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Srikanta Sastri (1904–1974) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and under M. H. Krishna, later serving on the faculty at the University of Mysore (~1930–1960).

Saba Mahmood (1961–2018) was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University. She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (from 2004).

Sabine Löhr is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, and worked as a student research assistant at the University of Hamburg.
